jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Privacy-Preserving Digital Wallets
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

The PhD project will design, implement and analyze privacy-preserving protocols for digital identity wallets, such as the EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet. The focus is on how cryptographic tools like zero-knowledge proofs and anonymous credentials can deliver selective disclosure, pseudonymity and unlinkability in practice, and on the privacy and security risks that arise when wallets are integrated into public and private services. A central question is how to balance strong privacy guarantees against security and usability. The proposed solutions will be evaluated both through security analysis and through user studies.

The position will run for four years, including teaching duties. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Discipline, and the workplace is in Trondheim.
About the project
The position is part of the project Cryptology and social life: Sovereignty, security and society meet digital wallets, funded by NTNU. The overall project goal is to develop knowledge, methodologies and competencies that strengthen Norway's ability to deploy and maintain secure, privacy-preserving and democratically aligned digital identity wallets. The challenges are interdisciplinary, cutting across issues of digital sovereignty, identity management and security technologies. This project will strengthen Norway's societal resilience by treating digital identity as a problem to be secured technologically, organizationally and culturally at once.

You will work closely with the three other PhD candidates in the project, in particular the candidate developing quantum-safe verifiable credentials. The user studies will be carried out together with the candidates studying the societal and organizational aspects of digital wallets.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the research group NTNU Applied Cryptology Lab (NaCl)
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching duties in relevant courses at the department
• Other career-promoting work
 Some changes to your work duties may occur after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the IE faculty's Doctoral Programme in Information Security and Communication Technology, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant master's degree in information security, cryptology, computer science, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than August 31, 2027.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in English
• Ability to perform research in a cross-disciplinary environment
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Documented experience with applied cryptography or privacy-enhancing technologies
• Knowledge of digital identity and verifiable credential systems, such as the EUDI Wallet
• Interest in and/or documented experience with usable security and privacy, or with human aspects related privacy-enhancing technologies, security, cryptography or other related areas 
• Programming skills and experience with implementing cryptographic protocols
• Relevant publication activities will be considered an advantage
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian languagePersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) 
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 4 years, of which 3 years are dedicated to the doctoral work and 1 year to career promotion work, such as teaching. The planned start date is August 2027.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Information Security and Communication Technology within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for bachelor's and master's degrees
• Curriculum Vitae (CV) with an overview of relevant experience 
• A short document with motivation and research statement on digital identities (2 pages)
• Copy of master's thesis. If you have not yet submitted your master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Possibly publications or other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates for relevant courses or skills outside of the educational program
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts of your education have been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both bachelor's and master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. 

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.

NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Tjerand Silde, email tjerand.silde@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR consultant Julie Lindland, email: julie.lindland@ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 20.11.2026

Candidates need expertise and interest in qualitative, interpretative and critical research methods as the work will entail working empirically with data collection from a wide set of stakeholders, drawing on interviews, observations and document analysis.

In this position, you will conduct research as part of the interdisciplinary project Cryptology and social life: Sovereignty, security and society meet digital wallets,  while achieving your doctorate degree. In this manner, you will gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education, research and other sectors requiring analytic skills, both within and outside academia. 

The position is situated within NTNU’s interdisciplinary area “A more resilient society” (“Et mer motstandsdyktig samfunn”), and affiliated with the interdisciplinary research project “Cryptology and social life” and NTNU’s interdisciplinary team “Democratic resilience” (Demokratisk motstandskraft). You will also become part of the research groups “Information systems and  computer-human interaction, ISCHI” and become a member of our vibrant research community with seminars, guests and visits.Thus, the position offers excellent opportunities for academic development, research collaboration, conference participation, international publication, and engagement with societal actors.

About the project
The PhD position is part of a group of four PhD’s forming the core of the NTNU funded interdisciplinary project “Cryptology and social life: Sovereignty, security and society meet digital wallets, combining information systems, STS, sociology, ethnography, and cryptology perspectives.  

The EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet is currently being deployed, with the intention to provide citizens with easier and expanded access to public and private services. Digital identity wallets will potentially become a critical socio-technical infrastructure also in Norway, and raises challenges related to issues such as privacy, fairness, stakeholder engagement and securityi. On this background the project's overall goal is to develop knowledge, methodologies and competencies that strengthen Norway's ability to deploy and maintain secure, privacy-preserving and democratically aligned digital identity wallets. Truly interdisciplinary, the challenges cut across issues of digital sovereignty, identity management, security technologies, and sociotechnical practices and imaginaries. Presently, critical, digital infrastructures are strongly dependent on foreign technology platforms, which limits the options for maintaining national and democratic control and accountabilityi.  Safe, digital identities are part of the critical infrastructure of our everyday societies. They enable a wide set of public and private services (cf. DigDir for Norwegian context). However, existing solutions and infrastructures for digital identites come with several challenges including but not limited to the following.

Many are operated and controlled by corporate entities typically from Big Tech. Having our critical, digital infrastructures dependent on Big Tech make them vulnerable hence undermines our digital sovereignty. While sufficient up till now, the type of security methods and technology in widespread use today are not quantum-safe, i.e., they are vulnerable to breaches with the advent of working quantum algorithms. To illustrate, the widely used RSA public key scheme underpinning many existing solutions including Norway’s BankID is not quantum safe. 

EUID involves the standardisation and coordination across countries in Europe with diverging existing solutions, experiences and expectations, which suggests that actually achieving comprehensive standardisation could be challenging.

The present PhD project is to analyse the technical, political, institutional and cultural conditions for digital wallets in a Norwegian context.  More specifically, important aspects of the PhD project are to understand: (i) the ecosystem (‘infrastructure’, ‘assemblage’) of existing solutions, practices and habits where new, digital wallets are to fit, (ii) the historic evolution of digital identity infrastructures (partly extending, partly substituting, partly competing with alternatives) and (iii) a comparative perspective contrasting Norway’s experience with relevant other European efforts.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Computer Science (IDI) at NTNU in Trondheim has a vacancy for a PhD Candidate in machine learning (four-year position). The topic of the PhD is machine learning for temporal and spatiotemporal data, that is, time series, including multivariate time series observed on the nodes and edges of a graph, with a focus on forecasting and on detecting disruptions. The position is part of STRIDE, an interdisciplinary NTNU project on the resilience of transport systems (see About the project), and transport networks are the main testbed.

Forecasting models are usually trained on data from normal operating conditions. When a disruption, such as a closed link, a capacity limit or a sudden change in demand, moves a network into a regime that is rare or absent in the training data, their performance degrades, and such events are often too rare to learn from directly. The PhD will develop deep learning methods that forecast reliably under this kind of distribution shift, and that can detect and locate disruptions from the observed data.

Possible research directions include:

• time-series foundation models, including pretraining on synthetic data from simulated dynamical systems, to handle events that are rare in real data
• spatiotemporal graph neural networks that model how disruptions propagate through a network
• anomaly detection and localization of disruptions in time series on graphs
The exact research focus will be defined together with the candidate. We expect the results to be published at leading machine learning conferences and journals.

The main supervisor will be Associate Professor Massimiliano Ruocco, with co-supervisors from the STRIDE team.

This is an interdisciplinary research project involving researchers in transport modelling, artificial intelligence, operations research, civil engineering, and science and technology studies. The project studies how transport systems respond to disruptions and how modelling and decision-support methods can strengthen resilience across planning, response, and recovery. The PhD candidate will work closely with three other PhD candidates studying interdependent hazards, data-driven modelling of multimodal transport, and the societal dimensions of resilience and total defense.

The Institute of Marine Research (IMR) offers a 3-year postdoctoral position as part of the MORSE (“Models supporting practical restoration of habitats and species in Europe’s seas”) research project funded by Horizon Europe. jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Political Science - Norway and the EU
jobs.description:
About the position 
ARENA Centre for European Studies at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) in political science or another relevant social science discipline. The position is for a period of three years, with no teaching or other required duties. 

The place of work is ARENA Centre for European Studies, University of Oslo.
 
ARENA is an interdisciplinary research centre at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. Since 1994, the centre has studied political, security, economic, legal and social integration, transformation and cooperation in Europe. ARENA has extensive experience in coordinating international research projects and networks funded by European and Norwegian institutions. 

The centre has around 30 academic and four administrative staff. More information about ARENA is available here.
More about the position 
Europe is being reshaped by war, geopolitical rivalry and a renewed enlargement agenda. As the EU's rules and decisions reach further beyond its borders, Norway faces key questions about alignment, influence and democratic control. Norway is one of the most closely integrated non-member states. That makes it an important case for understanding what it means to be part of European integration without being a member of the Union.

ARENA is looking for a PhD Research Fellow who wants to write a dissertation on Norway's relationship with the EU. The successful candidate will develop and carry out their own doctoral project in a research environment with long experience of studying European integration and its consequences for countries both inside and outside the Union.

We expect theoretically informed empirical studies and particularly welcome projects that take a comparative approach, but single-case studies of Norway are also welcome. Examples of comparisons could include comparing and contrasting Norway with other associated or third countries (such as Iceland, Switzerland or the United Kingdom), EU member states or candidate countries. Comparisons across policy areas are also welcome. We are open to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches.

Relevant research areas could include, but are not limited to:

• Norway's association model: Projects could for example address how the EEA Agreement and Norway's many other agreements with the EU shape Norwegian politics, public administration and regulation, or how they compare with those of comparable EU member or affiliated states. Projects could look at Norway's room for manoeuvre and influence vis-à-vis the EU, at questions of democratic legitimacy and control, or at how the association model is evolving as the EU changes. 
• Justice and home affairs: Projects could for example address Norway's participation in Schengen, European migration and asylum policy, border management, or police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. Projects could study how EU developments in these fields affect Norwegian policies, institutions and societal security, possibly compared with other associated or member countries.
We are looking for candidates with interesting and relevant research ideas, strong theoretical and analytical skills, and solid methodological competence. The project proposal should combine clear theoretical and empirical ambitions with a realistic and feasible research design.
Responsibilities
The appointment as a PhD Research Fellow at ARENA is for a period of three years, with no compulsory duties. As a fellow, you will be based at ARENA Centre for European Studies’ premises in Gaustadalléen, Oslo. Presence at the unit is a requirement. 

You will be admitted to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo.

This is a full-time position commencing in the winter or spring of 2027. You will have access to office space, equipment, and services, as well as resources for fieldwork and conference participation as needed.
What skills are important in this role?
Required selection criteria

• Grades placing the candidate in the top tier of the field (this also applies to the master's thesis)
• The master's degree must include relevant training in research design and methodology
• The master's thesis must correspond to a minimum workload of six months, i.e., 30 ECTS credits
• 
Excellent oral and written English proficiency is required

ARENA’s working language is English, and therefore, fluency in oral and written English is required. As Norway’s relationship with the EU is central to the position, Norwegian sources will be important, making good proficiency in Norwegian (or another Scandinavian language) an advantage.
 
Personal suitability

• You must be able to work independently and in a structured manner.

• You should possess good collaborative skills and demonstrate the ability, willingness, and commitment to contribute to the development of the research field.

• 
You should be able to take initiative and wish to participate actively in an international and interdisciplinary research team.

Appointment as a research fellow requires admission to a doctoral programme, or a binding agreement regarding admission. 

Application for admission to a PhD programme must normally be submitted within three months of the start of the research project leading to the PhD degree. 
Basis for assessment
In the assessment of candidates, particular emphasis will be placed on:

Personal qualities and motivation will be taken into consideration.

The centre combines Ukrainian combat experience with European standards. It will train, test and demonstrate unmanned systems for armed forces, the Home Guard, government agencies and industry.

We are looking for an experienced military leader who can build the centre from the ground up and make it operational. This person will represent the centre to the Norwegian defence and drone communities. Head of Centre will lead the team of pilots and instructors, and make sure training, testing and demonstrations are delivered safely and to a high standard. Flying personally is a strong advantage, but it is not required.

In this role, you will:

• 
Launch and lead the centre: set up the organisation, recruit the team, plan operations and handle safety and daily running.

• 
Recruit, lead and support the pilots and instructors who deliver training, test flights and customer demonstrations.

• 
Oversee course content, instructor standards and quality of delivery.

• 
Build relationships with the Armed Forces, Home Guard, defence procurement and research bodies, ranges and industry.

• 
Work closely with Ukrainian instructors and international partners.

• 
Make sure all activity follows aviation, security and export-control rules.

Who we are looking for:

• 
Former Norwegian Armed Forces officer or senior NCO with approximately 10+ years of service, including significant command or leadership responsibility. Background in the Army, Special Forces, ISR, artillery, or air defence is preferred.

• 
Demonstrated experience establishing and delivering new military units, capabilities, training programs, exercises, or operational projects. Ideally from concept through implementation.

• 
Proven ability to lead specialist teams and take responsibility for planning, personnel, resources, budgets, delivery, and results.

• 
Experience designing, organizing, or leading military training, courses, exercises, or capability-development programs.

• 
Current or recently held security clearance under the Norwegian Security Act at minimum SECRET/NATO SECRET, with willingness to undergo renewed security vetting. Must demonstrate a high level of integrity and discretion when handling sensitive information.

• 
An active professional network within the Norwegian Armed Forces, Home Guard, Special Forces community, defence industry, test and evaluation environments, or relevant government agencies.

• 
Hands-on experience operating small tactical drones and FPV systems is highly desirable, ideally including instructor experience. Candidates without prior flying experience must be willing to learn. Experience with drone or counter-UAS units, programs, procurement, or capability development is an advantage.

• 
Familiarity with BVLOS operations, night and thermal flying, and drone operations in GPS-denied or electronic-warfare environments is preferred. Knowledge of EU civil drone qualifications—such as A1/A3, A2, and STS—or SORA risk assessments is an advantage.

• 
Experience with test and evaluation, customer demonstrations, defense-industry collaboration, multinational or NATO operations, or Ukraine-related programs is desirable. Familiarity with export-control requirements and licensing for training foreign nationals on military technology is an advantage.

• 
Native-level Norwegian and fluent English are required, together with a willingness to travel regularly within Europe. The successful candidate should be credible with soldiers, senior officers, and commercial customers; be structured, proactive, and comfortable building new capabilities; and demonstrate respect for Ukrainian combat experience.

What we offer:

• 
An opportunity to join a growing technology company at an exciting stage of development

• 
Strategic role with high impact

• 
Meaningful responsibility and direct influence on products and processes

• 
A collaborative and international working environment

• 
Professional development and career growth opportunities

• 
Competitive compensation and benefits package

We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Economic Officer at the Embassy of Israel to Norway and Iceland
jobs.description:
About the Job

The Embassy of Israel to Norway and Iceland is seeking a dedicated and proactive Economic Officer. The primary goal of this position is to promote bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Israel and Norway, as well as to handle, guide, and assist Israeli businesses looking to establish themselves or expand into the Norwegian market.

Working closely with the embassy's diplomatic staff and relevant stakeholders, you will play a key role in fostering commercial ties, supporting trade delegations, and bridging the gap between Israeli innovation and Norwegian industry. As part of the Political Department at the embassy you will be expected to also contribute to other tasks that the department handles.

Central Tasks Include, but are not limited to:

● Trade Promotion: Actively work to expand commercial, industrial, and technological collaboration between Norwegian and Israeli companies.

● Business Assistance: Provide guidance, logistical support, and strategic advice to Israeli businesses, startups, and entrepreneurs seeking to establish operations or partnerships in Norway.

● Network Building: Establish and maintain a strong professional network with Norwegian businesses, industry associations, investors, and governmental bodies.

● Analysis & Reporting: Monitor and analyze economic trends, market developments, and business opportunities within the Norwegian market to prepare decision-making briefs for the diplomatic team.

● Coordination & Events: Coordinate trade delegations, B2B meetings, seminars, and promotional events showcasing Israeli technology and commerce.

● Inquiries: Handle commercial inquiries from both Israeli and Norwegian companies seeking market entry or partnership opportunities.

Qualifications and Experience

● Relevant higher education (Bachelor's or Master's degree) in economics, business administration, international trade, finance, or a related field.

● Relevant professional experience in business development, trade promotion, B2B sales, or project management.

● Excellent written and oral communication skills in both Norwegian and English.

● In-depth understanding of the Norwegian business landscape, regulatory framework, and economic environment.

● Strong interest in international trade and fostering bilateral economic relations.

Personal Characteristics

● Proactive, independent, and self-driven with a strong sense of initiative.

● Excellent interpersonal and networking skills, with the ability to build and maintain professional relationships.

● Solution-minded and commercially oriented.

● Analytical mindset with the ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced diplomatic environment.

● A passion for Israel and strengthening the Israel-Norway economic relationship.

Application Details

● Salary: Determined based on educational background and experience.

● Application Process: Please submit your CV and a short cover letter to: ambassador-assistant@oslo.mfa.gov.il

● Note: Candidates must be based in or willing to relocate to Oslo and cannot hold Israeli citizenship.

• Industrial salmon filleting and trimming
• Fish processing and seafood production
• Preparing and handling fresh fish on production lines
• Packing, sorting and quality control in seafood processing facilities
• Working with industrial seafood production equipment

Relevant experience from a fish processing plant or seafood factory is essential. We are primarily looking for candidates who know the production environment and can contribute from day one.

Experience from restaurants og hotel environments does not meet the requirements for these positions.

• Filleting and trimming salmon and other seafood

• Packing, sorting and inspecting finished products

• Following HACCP procedures and production routines
• Keeping workstations and production areas clean and organised
• Internal logistics, packing and palleting salmon

• Competitive salary and working conditions
• Flexible start up, this year og early next year.

• Training and onboarding
• Possibility of extended or long-term assignments for candidates relocating to the Oslo region who fits most criterias.

You should:

• Have at least 6–12 months of relevant experience from industrial seafood production, preferably salmon filleting, altnerativley poultry or meat.
• Be comfortable working with fresh fish in a chilled production environment
• Be able to work efficiently while maintaining high quality and hygiene standards
• Be willing to work in the Oslo region
• Speak English; Norwegian language at high level is not required, but an advantage with basic norwegian.

Candidates currently living in Western Norway or Northern Norway are encouraged to apply, especially if they have experience from established seafood processing plants.

We review applications continuously and contact relevant candidates for interviews at our office or per Teams
